subject: PoC / Trial plan — Deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: PoC recap & proposed trial plan (deployment mode discussion)

Thanks again for a productive call today, Alex — appreciate the clarity on Acme's objectives. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the PoC scope: 

Call summary:
- Goal: evaluate Redwood to reduce per-token cost and improve latency for Acme's document summarization pipeline (internal docs + customer support transcripts).
- Key non-functional constraints: sub-300ms median inference latency for short prompts, data residency in US, expected sustained throughput ~250 requests/min with bursts to 800.
- Primary stakeholders: Alex Johnson (AI Platform), Priya Singh (Procurement, cc'd on next emails), Dev infra (we understand you'll nominate a contact).

Deployment-mode considerations (recommended path):
1) Hosted API (fastest): lowest onboarding friction, we can run a 2-week trial on Hosted to validate accuracy and baseline latency. Good for early model validation and evals.
2) Dedicated capacity: if throughput and predictable tail latency are top priorities, we can provision a dedicated GPU pool for the PoC to mirror production load. We can offer a short-duration reserved pool for PoC.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended only if Acme requires customer-managed networking or strict regulatory controls. We can scope this once success criteria are met.

Proposed PoC / trial plan (high level):
- Duration: 2 weeks (validation) + optional 2-week stress/throughput test on Dedicated (if requested).
- Success criteria (examples):
  * 95th percentile latency < 600ms for production prompts (goal: 300ms median)
  * Throughput: sustain 250 req/min with peak bursts to 800 without dropping below SLOs
  * Cost: per-token unit cost improvement vs current baseline >= 20%
  * Functional parity: generated summaries match baseline quality on provided eval set (we'll run a blind A/B).
- Redwood owners: Ben Carter (sales / PoC lead), Marissa Cole (CS), Dev Patel (solutions / infra).
- Acme owners: Alex Johnson (PoC sponsor), Dev infra point (TBD), Priya Singh (procurement).

Attachments: I attached a short SOW (Redwood_PoC_SOW.pdf) and a network checklist (network_requirements.xlsx) — please review and flag anything missing.

Next steps / asks: 
1) Confirm PoC kickoff window — I propose Aug 17 start (allowing a few days for sign-off).
2) Confirm which deployment mode you want to start with (Hosted preferred for speed; we can then run bench on Dedicated if you want to validate production SLAs).
3) Share the infra contact for VPC/network work (we'll only need this if you opt for Dedicated with customer network peering or Private VPC).
4) Priya — happy to get procurement questions answered; attaching SOW for review and DocuSign when ready.

If that looks good I’ll send a short kickoff agenda + calendar invite.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: PoC recap & proposed trial plan (deployment mode discussion)

Thanks Ben — useful recap. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) Deployment mode preference: our preference at first glance is Dedicated capacity for the PoC. We want to understand tail latency under load — Hosted is fine for functional validation but we'd like a short Dedicated run during the PoC to validate production behavior. Can Redwood support a short reserved pool (2 weeks) for testing?

2) Data residency & security: US-only residency is mandatory. We also need clarification on logging & retention (how long request/response logs are stored, ability to disable). Please have security/CS provide the SOC2 and data handling FAQ.

3) Timeline: Aug 17 kickoff works for us, depending on procurement sign-off.

4) Procurement: Priya is looped in — she will handle contracting. Priya, feel free to add any procurement-specific asks here.

Matt (our infra lead) will be the technical contact for network peering and we’ll introduce him once procurement confirms the trial.

— Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC recap & proposed trial plan (deployment mode discussion)

Appreciate the quick response, Alex — happy to confirm details. Short answers inline: 

1) Dedicated reserved pool: yes, we can provision a short-duration dedicated GPU pool for the PoC (2 weeks) — we'll need a brief capacity reservation and the network peering details if you want private peering. For the initial validation we can start on Hosted immediately and schedule the Dedicated test in the second week.

2) Data & logs: we store request/response logs for 30 days by default; we can offer a reduced retention or disabling of response payload retention for the PoC. SOC 2 and our security FAQ are available — Marissa will share the links in a follow-up.

3) Timeline & milestones (proposed):
  - Aug 17: Kickoff, access provisioning, baseline test on Hosted with your eval set.
  - Aug 19-21: Functional validation & quality A/B tests on Hosted.
  - Aug 22-28: Dedicated reserved pool stress/throughput run (if you opt-in).
  - Aug 29: PoC closeout, measurement vs success criteria and recommendation for production mode.

4) Success criteria (confirming): 95th percentile latency < 600ms, sustain throughput target, cost delta >= 20% improvement, quality parity on eval set. If you want, we can add a simple SLA burn-down metric during the Dedicated run.

5) Stakeholders: Please confirm Matt's email for network peering and Priya for procurement. For Redwood: Marissa will set up the monitoring dashboard and CS attachments; Dev Patel will be your infra contact to walk through any firewall/peering requirements.

Action items for Acme (please):
- Confirm kickoff date (proposed Aug 17).
- Confirm Matt (infra) contact and Priya for procurement.
- Review attached SOW and return with any redlines — we can expedite DocuSign once procurement is ready.

I’ll go ahead and draft the kickoff agenda and a short runbook (redwood-trial-config.yml) and share via the Drive link.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Ben
